title: Biophilic Design as an Important Bridge for Sustainable Interaction between Humans and the Environment: Based on Practice in Chinese Healthcare Space
research_question: This research analyzes the application mode and existing problems of 12 healthcare spaces in China from the perspective of biophilic design and proposes suitable design solutions. The goal of this study was to present ideas for healthy and efficient space environment design and to inspire sustainable environmental design for future healthcare environments.

participants.description: 240 respondents (55% men, 45% women; 30% aged 25-30, 29% aged 31-40, 41% aged 41 or older; 57.5% patients, 24.2% hospital staff, 18.3% others) from various countries including China, participating in a survey on biophilic design patterns in healthcare environments. The case study involved 12 national hospitals in China.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: 12 national hospitals in China with floor areas of 50,000 m² or more, focusing on high pedestrian flow nodes (lobby reception, registration/payment, waiting area, corridor, CT room, inpatient ward, hospital lift).
Photos of each scenario (biophilic design patterns in healthcare environments) were included in the questionnaire to enhance respondents' comprehension.
Transformed medical space environment designs (Kaiyi Hospital's Hall, waiting area, ward, healing garden) created using SketchUp, Lumion10, Enscape3.0, and AutoCAD2020.

measures.instrument: 27 survey items in three patterns (direct nature experience, indirect nature experience, experience mode of natural sense of space) with photos and effect descriptions, rated on a Likert scale (presumably 1-5, given means).

findings.mechanism: Direct access to nature and natural light provides restorative benefits, reducing stress and improving mood.
findings.quote: a small patio-style garden can be added to the waiting area, introducing natural light through the patio and floor-to-ceiling windows so that patients can enjoy the external beauty even when they are inside.

findings.quote: the walls can be painted in a natural-elements design, and vegetation can be put to the room to help the patient relax.

findings.antecedent: Natural patterns (sky, woods) on CT room ceiling, natural sounds (fountains, streams, waves, birdsong, rain)
findings.consequent: Patient soothing through audio and visual stimulation
findings.mechanism: Multisensory natural stimuli can distract from stress and promote relaxation, especially when patients are supine.
findings.quote: natural patterns such as the sky or woods can be added to the ceiling, while natural sounds such as fountains, streams, waves, birdsong, and rain can be added to soothe the patient through a combination of audio and visual stimulation.

findings.antecedent: Natural elements (plants, animals like goldfish) and natural environment-shaped walls (beehive) in wards
findings.consequent: Beautification of wards, unique natural element in landscape
findings.mechanism: Incorporating diverse natural elements enhances the aesthetic appeal and creates a more engaging environment.
findings.quote: natural elements can be used to beautify the wards by including appropriate plants and animals, such as green buckets and goldfish. Create a unique natural element in the landscape by forming the walls in the shape of a natural environment, such as a beehive.

findings.antecedent: Screens with pulleys (rigid material) instead of fabric bed curtains in multi-person wards
findings.consequent: Improved space division, unobstructed flow of space
findings.mechanism: Rigid, movable screens offer better privacy control and maintain a sense of openness compared to fabric curtains.
findings.quote: instead of bed curtains, screens with pulleys can be used. Screens of rigid material are more capable of dividing space than fabric bedroom curtains, and the pulleys ensure that the flow of space is unobstructed.

findings.antecedent: Ward unit with zigzag plane, green platforms in recesses, and external multilevel healing garden
findings.consequent: Direct contact with nature, enhanced healing properties of interior space
findings.mechanism: Integrated natural views and direct access to nature provide restorative benefits and promote healing.
findings.quote: The ward unit adopts a zigzag plane, and green platforms are arranged in the recesses in the plane so that there is a natural landscape outside each window. Combined with the external multilevel healing garden, patients on each floor have the opportunity to have direct contact with nature and use the 'direct experience mode' with nature in the biophilic design to enhance the healing properties of the interior space.

findings.antecedent: Windows with removable louvers in wards
findings.consequent: Maximized daylight, minimized glare, shielding from low-angle sunlight, sense of perspective
findings.mechanism: Controllable daylighting improves visual comfort, reduces glare, and provides a sense of control and connection to the outside.
findings.quote: The windows also feature removable louvers to maximize daylight and minimize glare, shielding patients from low-angle sunlight in the morning and evening. And a forward-facing eave can be added to the window to give the patient a sense of perspective.

findings.antecedent: Multifaceted composite landscape system in healing gardens (different scales/types of nonirritating odor plants, geometric cuts, microtopographical enclosures)
findings.consequent: Creation of spatial places with different experiential sensations, increased complexity and connectivity, sense of mystery, sense of refuge
findings.mechanism: Diverse and complex natural elements provide varied sensory experiences, promoting exploration, curiosity, and feelings of safety and refuge.
findings.quote: First, a multifaceted composite landscape system can be introduced into the garden, such as different scales and types of nonirritating odor plants, to create spatial places with different experiential sensations and to increase complexity and connectivity. The use of plants and geometric cuts and microtopographical enclosures creates a private and secluded place that adds a sense of mystery and provides a sense of refuge for patients.

findings.antecedent: Tree-shrouded paths leading to distant views and landmarks in healing gardens
findings.consequent: Increased depth and coherence to space, control of emotions, restoration of focus, sense of 'distance'
findings.mechanism: Providing clear pathways and distant views supports wayfinding, reduces cognitive load, and offers opportunities for mental restoration.
findings.quote: Tree-shrouded paths lead people's eyes to distant views and landmarks, giving depth and coherence to the space of this journey. This atmosphere allows people to control their emotions and restore their focus by providing a momentary getaway, a sense of 'distance.'

findings.antecedent: Dynamic water features (cascading water, streams, water mists, fogs) in healing gardens
findings.consequent: Creation of natural and dynamic water ecology, increased vitality, increased air humidity, comfortable microclimate, pleasant emotional experience
findings.mechanism: Dynamic water features provide multisensory stimulation, improve microclimate, and evoke positive emotional responses.
findings.quote: Dynamic water features such as cascading water and streams can create a natural and dynamic water ecology and bring vitality to patients. Landscapes such as water mists and fogs can increase the humidity of the air in the hospital environment and create a microclimate of comfortable spaces. Patients can interact with the water features to create a pleasant emotional experience.

findings.antecedent: Introduction of animal therapy/animal elements in healing gardens
findings.consequent: Promotion of interaction between people and nature, increased emotional connection to place, relief of physical exhaustion and pain, increased sense of belonging
findings.mechanism: Interaction with animals can reduce stress, provide comfort, and foster a sense of connection and belonging.
findings.quote: the introduction of animal therapy, the inclusion of animal elements, can promote interaction between people and nature and increase the emotional connection of the place. The interaction and play of patients with animals can increase patients' sense of belonging to the hospital space, which in turn relieves patients' physical exhaustion and pain.

mechanisms: Biophilic design improves the quality of environments and the health of users by restoring the interaction between buildings and nature.
Nature's therapeutic effect on physical and mental health operates through numerous direct and indirect relationships.
Biophilic design interprets the relationship between nature, space environment, and human health from biological and psychological perspectives.

Natural materials improve optical effects (by absorbing more light than they reflect) and have a favorable impact on olfactory comfort (through essential oils), creativity, overall health, and the immune system.
Biophilic design, based on the biophilic nature of human beings, boosts human health, cognition, and productivity.
Continuous stimulation of the human body via various sensory inputs (vision, hearing, touch, smell) to natural components enhances health.

Natural space experience models create immersive natural experiences through artificial environments, alleviating mental fatigue, promoting refocusing, intelligent recovery, and increasing staff motivation and communication.

Emotional attachment to the environment, fostered by biophilic design, helps patients develop positive emotions, relaxation, willingness to integrate into treatment, and confidence in the treatment plan.
Systematic use of several natural components is more effective than individual elements for creating a sense of natural space and environment.
Multisensory complex stimulation by natural elements is more attractive than single-sense stimulation.
Elements of nature that attract active participation and physical activity are more influential than those for static appreciation.

Interaction with animals (e.g., fish, animal therapy) enhances cognitive and reactive abilities, provides relaxing effects, and offers healing space, especially for parents with children by diverting attention from stress.
implementation_implications: Biophilic design processes must carefully select natural elements and use highly controlled design methods to avoid increased infection risk and physiological burden.
To ensure correct biophilic design in healthcare, patient safety, and avoidance of additional harm, design must be prudent and effective.
Optimize the interaction mode between direct or indirect natural elements and people.
Increase the emotional connection of the place and provide interactive places for shelter and lookout.
Realize systematic compounding with real and diverse designs, objectively and realistically displaying diversified natural elements.
Design should focus on the roof interface, which is often overlooked but frequently sighted by patients.

For spaces with spatial limits (e.g., imaging centers), indirect natural experience models using materials (logs for tactile), electronic media (audiovisual), and natural scents (olfactory) can create comprehensive fake natural experiences.

limitations: The biophilic design research system for medical spaces is not yet perfect, and application norms and methods need further optimization.
Many existing designs in China fall short of biophilic principles, indicating a lack of systematic application of theories, models, and procedures.
Implementing biophilic design is challenging in many developing countries and regions due to economic factors and research limitations.
The study primarily identifies existing problems and proposes design solutions, lacking empirical validation of the proposed designs.

paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: Since the COVID-19 epidemic, there has been an increased need for well-being and sustainable development, making biophilic design in hospital environments even more significant. However, after investigation, it was found that in many countries including China, the biophilic design of some hospitals is seriously absent, while other parts have the integration of biophilic design, but the standardization and recognition are not high. By restoring the interaction between buildings and nature, biophilic design improves the quality of environments and the health of users. The basic theoretical framework of environmental psychology is followed in this research. The health promotion mechanism, applicable natural features, and relative health advantages of hospital space and environment biophilic design are first investigated. Furthermore, according to the current status of biophilic design applications in the 12 hospitals that have the closest interaction between people and the environment. Combined with the professional and functional requirements of the healthcare spaces and the users’ special demands, we propose appropriate update design methods. The goal of this study was to present ideas for healthy and efficient space environment design and to inspire sustainable environmental design for future healthcare environments.

crossref_abstract: Since the COVID-19 epidemic, there has been an increased need for well-being and sustainable development, making biophilic design in hospital environments even more significant. However, after investigation, it was found that in many countries including China, the biophilic design of some hospitals is seriously absent, while other parts have the integration of biophilic design, but the standardization and recognition are not high. By restoring the interaction between buildings and nature, biophilic design improves the quality of environments and the health of users. The basic theoretical framework of environmental psychology is followed in this research. The health promotion mechanism, applicable natural features, and relative health advantages of hospital space and environment biophilic design are first investigated. Furthermore, according to the current status of biophilic design applications in the 12 hospitals that have the closest interaction between people and the environment. Combined with the professional and functional requirements of the healthcare spaces and the users’ special demands, we propose appropriate update design methods. The goal of this study was to present ideas for healthy and efficient space environment design and to inspire sustainable environmental design for future healthcare environments.
